title: Implement Configurable Image Resizing Interpolation
description: The PixUtility Vision Stack currently uses a hardcoded interpolation method (Bilinear) for all image resizing operations during data preprocessing. This task requires you to make this behavior configurable. You will introduce a new setting in the configuration file, update the core image processing logic to use this setting, and finally, expose it as a command-line flag to override the configuration for specific runs. This task will require modifications across the configuration, core library, and command-line interface, testing your ability to trace data flow and functionality through the C codebase over multiple development sessions.

project_spec.name: PixUtility Vision Stack
project_spec.description:
PixUtility Vision Stack is a medium-scale, C-based computer-vision utility that exposes a Swiss-army-knife collection of visual analysis tools (resize, denoise, detect, classify, annotate) through a single CLI, a lightweight REST/gRPC micro-service, and a shared library.  Where typical vision projects concentrate on a single model or task, PixUtility is purposely built as a **general-purpose system utility** that sys-admins, DevOps engineers, and other applications can script or embed in larger pipelines. 

The codebase is organized as a strict **layered architecture**: (1) an I/O layer for image/video ingestion supporting files, stdin/stdout, and RTSP streams; (2) a preprocessing & feature-engineering layer that standardises colour spaces, crops, augments, and extracts domain-agnostic features; (3) a model layer hosting multiple ONNX/TFLite models with Factory-Pattern instantiation and Model-Registry versioning; (4) a service layer exposing gRPC/REST endpoints with Observer hooks for experiment tracking and model monitoring; and (5) a utility CLI layer offering Unix-style sub-commands (`pixutil detect`, `pixutil eval`, `pixutil tune`).  Integrated experiment tracking, automated hyper-parameter sweeps, and continuous model monitoring make the toolkit production-ready while maintaining the light footprint expected from a C utility.
